description:
How Did One Tiny World Kick Pluto Out?

Episode 106 of a daily journey through the universe. 🪐
We travel to Eris: discovered in 2005, about 27% more massive than Pluto, about 2,326 km wide, now about 96 times farther from the Sun than Earth, a 559-year orbit, its moon Dysnomia, and how it started the 2006 vote that made Pluto a dwarf planet.

➡️ Tomorrow, Episode 107: Next stop, Haumea. A dwarf planet shaped like an egg, with a ring.
Start from Episode 1 "Leaving Earth" on the channel.
Follow so you don't miss a stop. A new episode every day.

Narration: AI voice

#space #eris #astronomy #shorts #science #nasa

segments.text: How did one small, faraway world get Pluto kicked out of the planets?
In January twenty oh five, astronomers found a world far beyond Pluto. At first, it looked even bigger than Pluto.
segments.headline: Bigger than Pluto?

segments.text: It's named Eris, after the Greek goddess of discord. And it lived up to its name.
segments.headline: Goddess of discord

segments.text: If Eris wasn't a planet, then why was Pluto? In twenty oh six, astronomers voted on a new rule.
segments.headline: A big vote in 2006

segments.text: A planet must clear its own path around the Sun. Pluto and Eris don't. Both became dwarf planets.
Eris is almost the same width as Pluto, about two thousand three hundred kilometers. But it's about twenty-seven percent heavier.
Right now it's about ninety-six times farther from the Sun than Earth. One orbit takes five hundred and fifty-nine years.
It's so cold that its air may have frozen onto the ground as bright white frost.
segments.headline: Frozen air

segments.text: Its little moon, Dysnomia, helped scientists weigh it.
segments.headline: Its moon Dysnomia

segments.text: Tomorrow, a dwarf planet that spins so fast it got stretched into an egg. And it has a ring. Which part surprised you most? Tell me in the comments, and follow for tomorrow's stop.
